subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the bracketed idiom in the given sentence.

He bought (a baker's dozen) of biscuits.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3'** i.e. '**Thirteen'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A **baker's dozen** typically refers to a quantity of thirteen items.
 
• This **term originated from** the practice of bakers adding an extra item (usually a roll or bread loaf) to a dozen (12) to compensate for any potential shortfall due to loss or shrinkage during baking.
 
• So, when someone buys a baker's dozen of biscuits, they're purchasing **thirteen biscuits.**

Therefore, the** correct answer** is - '**Option 3'.**
